chunks: And it is narrated from al-Faḍl ibn Abī Qurrah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: These people say that the earnings of the teacher are illicit. So he said:

The enemies of Allah have lied. They only wanted that they should not teach their children the Qur'an. If a man were to give the teacher the blood-money of his child, it would be permissible for the teacher.

key_terms.أَعْدَاءُ ٱللَّهِ: the enemies of Allah, used here for those spreading this false claim
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money or legal compensation paid for a life
key_terms.كَسْبَ: earnings or income acquired through one's work
key_terms.ٱلْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, the subject being taught
key_terms.ٱلْمُعَلِّمِ: the teacher, specifically the one providing instruction

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to take payment for teaching the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects the claim that a teacher’s earnings are unlawful, especially in relation to teaching the Qur'an. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام declares such speech false and affirms the permissibility of compensating a teacher, emphasizing the value of Qur'anic instruction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3597 - It is reported from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurrah that he said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (as), "These people claim that the earnings of a teacher are unlawful."

Imam (as) replied: "The enemies of Allah (swt) have lied! They only intend to prevent their children from learning the Quran. If a man were to give the teacher the blood money of his child, it would be lawful for the teacher."
